…such a proposal, thereby soon weakening the feudatory princes, as Zhufu Yan did. This proposal both advanced the way of benevolence and filial piety and extinguished the first stirrings of rebellion. In what is called securing the house of Han as firmly as Mount Tai without outward agitation, Yan’s contribution was considerable indeed. I would not have expected someone versed in the arts of the diplomatic strategists, as Yan was, to devise such a plan. Some say, “Jia Yi had already proposed Yan’s policy.” Could it be that men skilled in strategy see things much alike?

During the decline of the late Tang, the regional military commands grew overbearing. In peaceful times they wielded great power and slighted the court; in times of trouble they relied on their powerful regional bases to coerce the Son of Heaven. There was no greater affliction in the realm. Later, someone proposed a plan to take control of the troops and regulate taxation, thereby eventually eliminating the power of the regional military commands: Zhao Pu. This plan both preserved the bonds of favor between ruler and ministers and ended the calamities of warfare. In what is called securing the realm as firmly as Mount Tai without outward agitation, Pu’s strategy was truly excellent. I would not have expected a bookish scholar of many schemes, as Pu was, to produce such a plan. Some say, “Wu Chongyin had already proposed Pu’s policy.” Could independently conceived ideas happen to coincide?

Then, in the reign of Dezong, the regional military commands defied imperial orders. He was determined to eliminate them, and the various commands feared his stern authority. At that time, Li Zhengji, Military Commissioner of Ziqing, submitted a memorial offering three hundred thousand in cash. He was testing the court through its acceptance or refusal. Dezong wished to accept, but feared being deceived by him; to reject the offer, however, would rebuff his overture. This was a matter of state policy…

可與執拗者並談與紹興之際宋室偏安

紹興之際，宋室偏安。於時以重兵守淮者，韓世忠也。世忠以所部兵少，乞摘張俊部趙密一將為助。時俊疑世忠吞已也，拒命不分。夫挾權相疑，欲服其心難矣。時趙忠簡處之，乃撥御前楊沂中一將，以益世忠之寡，而抽趙密入衛，以裒俊之多，俊始無辭。夫呼吸應變，張翕若神。如忠簡者，不吐不茹，可與拘曲者並論與？
之數君子者，或能銷禍亂於奸雄睥睨之秋，或能定謀議於反側危疑之際，或能决幾微於造次指顧之時。超然遠覽，謂之曰識可也；卓然先覺，謂之曰敏可也；確然自信，謂之曰斷可也。要皆所謂社稷之臣也。不然，使漢于諸侯也，以割削為辭，則七國之難作矣；宋于節鎮也，以征討為尚，
translation_en:
…one of the state’s Three Dukes. To treat a subordinate ruler’s minister in this way is excessive. Now that Li has approached us, he actually calls himself ‘Ningling.’ This is an official title in his own state; it is enough to address him by that title.” With just a few words spoken on the spur of the moment, the proper course of state policy was settled. Could someone like Pang Zhuangmin, so skilled in deliberation and decision, be spoken of in the same breath as the obstinate?
During the Shaoxing reign, the Song ruling house held sway over only part of the realm. At that time, Han Shizhong defended the Huai region with a large army. Finding the troops under his command too few, Shizhong requested that Zhao Mi, a commander serving under Zhang Jun, be detached to assist him. Jun suspected that Shizhong intended to swallow up his own forces [?], and refused the order to divide them. When men cling to power and suspect one another, it is difficult to win their willing obedience. Zhao Zhongjian handled the matter by assigning Yang Yizhong, a commander of the imperial forces, to reinforce Shizhong’s smaller army, while withdrawing Zhao Mi to serve in the imperial guard, thereby reducing Jun’s larger army. Only then did Jun have no grounds for objection. Responding to changing circumstances in a single breath, he expanded and contracted the forces with almost supernatural skill. Could someone like Zhongjian, who neither yielded before the strong nor bullied the weak, be discussed alongside men of narrow and rigid views?
These several gentlemen could avert calamity and disorder when treacherous men of ambition watched for an opening; settle deliberations amid unrest, danger, and uncertainty; or discern and decide the subtlest developments in moments of haste, in the time it takes to point or glance. Their ability to rise above immediate circumstances and see far ahead may be called discernment; their outstanding ability to perceive things before others may be called acuity; their firm confidence in their own judgment may be called decisiveness. In essence, all were what are called ministers who safeguard the altars of soil and grain. Otherwise, had the Han dealt with the feudal princes by insisting on reductions of their territories, the calamity of the Seven Kingdoms would have arisen; had the Song made punitive military expeditions its preferred means of dealing with the regional military commands, …

title: 隆慶元年順天府鄉試錄
text:
□□大之逆滋矣獻錢或受或不受則朝
廷可得而嘗矣乞粟或與或不與則宋可
得而覘矣名器假人則貴臣獲尊稱矣參
伍不設則驁將將有辭矣而國事何所賴
哉甚矣社稷之臣不多見也後之臨事者
吾惑焉有闇於大計懵於低昂眩於名實
以國事聽之天者有利害兩端是非首鼠
終始因仍倖一時國事之安者有自私用
智違衆拂經膠柱是非執中而無權者夫
===
以國事聽之天者無所處置者也倖一時
之安者苟於處置者也執中而無權者强
於處置者也無所處置則存亡立判矣可
謂識與苟於處置則昧於知變矣可謂敏
與强於處置則不免遺禍矣可謂斷與如
是而天下之大事去矣此豈愛國者之所
忍爲哉甚矣處事之難也抑人有稱物者
物始過衡則亟反之故權得無墮而衡得
無殆苟泄泄然徐而圖之是以卒致墮權

□夫之逆滋矣厭錢或受或不受則爭
廷可得而嘗矣乞粟或與或不與則求可
得而覬矣名器假人則貴臣獲尊稱矣參
伍不設則驁將有辭矣而國事何所賴
哉甚矣社稷之臣不多見也後之臨事者
吾惑焉有闇於大計情於低昂眩於名實
以國事聽之天者有利害兩端是非首鼠
終始因仍倖一時國事之安者有自私用
智違衆拂經膠柱是非執中而無權者夫
===
以國事聽之天者無所處置者也倖一時
之安者苟於處置者也執中而無權者強
於處置者也無所處置則存亡立判矣可
謂識與苟於處置則昧於知變矣可謂斂
與強於處置則不免遺禍矣可謂斷與如
是而天下之大事去矣此豈愛國者之所
忍爲哉甚矣處事之難也抑人有稱物者
物始過衡則亟反之故權得無墮而衡得
無殆苟泄泄然徐而圖之是以卒致墮權
punctuated:
□□大之逆滋矣。獻錢或受或不受，則朝廷可得而嘗矣；乞粟或與或不與，則宋可得而覘矣；名器假人，則貴臣獲尊稱矣；參伍不設，則驁將將有辭矣。而國事何所賴哉？甚矣，社稷之臣不多見也！後之臨事者，吾惑焉：有闇於大計，懵於低昂，眩於名實，以國事聽之天者；有利害兩端，是非首鼠，終始因仍，倖一時國事之安者；有自私用智，違衆拂經，膠柱是非，執中而無權者。夫以國事聽之天者，無所處置者也；倖一時之安者，苟於處置者也；執中而無權者，强於處置者也。無所處置，則存亡立判矣，可謂識與？苟於處置，則昧於知變矣，可謂敏與？强於處置，則不免遺禍矣，可謂斷與？如是而天下之大事去矣。此豈愛國者之所忍爲哉？甚矣，處事之難也！

抑人有稱物者，物始過衡，則亟反之，故權得無墮，而衡得無殆。苟泄泄然徐而圖之，是以卒致墮權
translation_en:
…the rebellion of □□大 [?] would have grown. If offerings of money were sometimes accepted and sometimes refused, the court could be put to the test; if requests for grain were sometimes granted and sometimes denied, the state of Song could be probed. If titles and insignia of rank were bestowed on others, powerful ministers would acquire exalted designations; if checks and cross-checks were not instituted, arrogant generals would have grounds for objection. On what, then, could the affairs of state depend? How rarely indeed do ministers who safeguard the state appear!

I am bewildered by those of later times who confront affairs. Some are ignorant of grand strategy, fail to understand the relative weight of things, are confused about names and realities, and leave affairs of state to Heaven. Some waver between advantage and harm, hesitate over right and wrong, follow established ways from beginning to end, and hope that affairs of state will remain peaceful for the moment. Some selfishly employ their cleverness, oppose the views of others and violate enduring principles, fix their judgments of right and wrong as rigidly as if gluing the bridges of a zither, and adhere to the mean without weighing circumstances.

Those who leave affairs of state to Heaven make no arrangements at all; those who hope for momentary peace are careless in their arrangements; those who adhere to the mean without weighing circumstances are inflexible in their arrangements. When no arrangements are made, survival or destruction is decided at once: can this be called discernment? When arrangements are careless, one fails to recognize changing circumstances: can this be called acuity? When arrangements are inflexible, one inevitably leaves calamity behind: can this be called decisiveness? In this way, the great affairs of the realm are lost. How could anyone who loves his country bear to act thus? How difficult indeed it is to manage affairs!

Consider someone weighing an object. As soon as the object tips the balance, he promptly corrects it, so that the weight does not fall and the beam is not imperiled. If he dallies and only slowly considers what to do, he thereby causes the weight eventually to fall…

title: 隆慶元年順天府鄉試錄
text:
而殆衡天下之事猶是也又人有理身者
或告之曰爾元憊矣爾氣衰矣毋勞爾形
毋摇爾精可以全生其人不怒則指以為
妄及一旦百疾暴發扁鵲望之驚走矣天
下之事猶是也是以貴識貴敏貴斷也故
曰以審勢者尚其識識不至事必無賴矣
以應變者尚其敏敏不至事必無賴矣以
裁幾者尚其斷斷不至事必無賴矣嗚呼
如偃如昔如祐甫如白如籍如鼎此六君
===
子者由此其選與愚生論世之餘敢繹所
聞如此若曰大受則非承學所敢及也謹
對
第五問
楊譽
同考試官知縣陳 批 經費不給司農告匱當
時之急務也塲中多勦陳言未聞至計子欲節其流以紓目前之意
欲定其制以善久遠之規是誠醫國之既治其標又理其本也豈非天下
之至計耶宜錄之以式多士

妄及一旦百疾景發扁鵲望之驚走矣天
下之事猶是也是以貴識貴敏貴斷也故

對
第五問
===
楊譽
同考試官知縣陳　批
時之急務也場中多勤陳言未聞至計子欲節其流以紓目前之急經費不給司農告匱當
欲定其制以善久遠之規是誠醫者之既治其標又理其本也豈非天下
之至計耶宜錄之以式多士
punctuated:
而殆衡。天下之事猶是也。又人有理身者，或告之曰：「爾元憊矣，爾氣衰矣，毋勞爾形，毋摇爾精，可以全生。」其人不怒，則指以為妄。及一旦百疾暴發，扁鵲望之驚走矣。天下之事猶是也。是以貴識、貴敏、貴斷也。故曰：以審勢者，尚其識，識不至，事必無賴矣；以應變者，尚其敏，敏不至，事必無賴矣；以裁幾者，尚其斷，斷不至，事必無賴矣。嗚呼！如偃，如昔，如祐甫，如白，如籍，如鼎，此六君子者，由此其選與？愚生論世之餘，敢繹所聞如此。若曰大受，則非承學所敢及也。謹對。
第五問
楊譽
同考試官知縣陳批：經費不給，司農告匱，當時之急務也。塲中多勦陳言，未聞至計。子欲節其流，以紓目前之意；欲定其制，以善久遠之規。是誠醫國之既治其標，又理其本也。豈非天下之至計耶？宜錄之，以式多士。
translation_en:
…and imperil the balance. The affairs of the realm are just like this. Again, consider a man tending to his health. Someone tells him: “Your vital essence is exhausted, and your vital energy is declining. Do not weary your body or agitate your essence; then you can preserve your life.” If the man does not become angry, he dismisses this as nonsense. But when a hundred ailments suddenly erupt one day, even Bian Que takes one look and flees in alarm. The affairs of the realm are just like this. That is why discernment, promptness, and decisiveness are prized. Thus I say: in assessing circumstances, discernment is paramount; without sufficient discernment, affairs will have nothing to rely upon. In responding to change, promptness is paramount; without sufficient promptness, affairs will have nothing to rely upon. In judging the first intimations of events, decisiveness is paramount; without sufficient decisiveness, affairs will have nothing to rely upon. Alas! Such men as Yan, Xi [?], Youfu, Bai, Ji, and Ding—were not these six gentlemen outstanding by virtue of these qualities? Having reflected on the affairs of past ages, I, an unworthy student, venture thus to elaborate upon what I have learned. As for bearing great responsibilities, that is beyond what a mere student dares presume to undertake. Respectfully submitted in reply.
Fifth Question
Yang Yu
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Magistrate: Expenditure exceeds available funds, and the Ministry of Revenue reports depleted resources: this is an urgent concern of the present time. Many in the examination hall have merely copied stale formulations; no truly sound plan has been heard. You propose to curb the outflow of funds with the intention of relieving the immediate difficulty, and to establish a fixed system as a sound plan for the distant future. This is indeed to heal the state by treating both its symptoms and its underlying condition. Is this not a supremely sound plan for the realm? It should be recorded as a model for the many candidates.

執事以經費不給，司農告匱，而欲諸生根極弊原，敷陳可久之道。此國家之大計，廟堂所孜孜日夜而求者，蓋非一日矣。曩者黠虜瞷邊吏之不戒，闖我近郊，中外大恐。於是握鈴者委於力之不敵，徵各邊技擊入衞，且廣募材勇爲新兵，歲增度支費數十萬計。先是，各邊以烽警之不時，屯鹽利失，無以自資給，往往祈助内帑，度支業已病矣。謀損之不得也，及是則更浩衍，遂大困。計臣謀士思爲國家建長久之策，聚首而談，持籌而畫。内之所訏謨條議，外之所建置興革，汰冗員，節浮費，廣開納，括贖金，督逋負，細至驛遞曆紙，靡不徵估内輸，可謂極矣。然所入終不

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Right Companion to the Heir Apparent: 〔The fiscal administration is hard pressed by provisioning the frontier. If frontier defenses are adequately supplied, the state's〕〔finances can enjoy greater latitude. You can identify and explain the sources of abuse, and moreover propose restoring military agricultural colonies and the salt system as a lasting measure. Surely you understand the pressing affairs of the age!〕

Comment by Examiner Ding, Right Admonisher to the Heir Apparent: 〔On this policy question concerning state finances, candidates in the examination hall have mostly plagiarized stale〕〔arguments, with scarcely anything worth reading. You alone can probe the abuses to their very source and set forth the best measures. Can you be regarded as merely a student of the classics? Select this answer at once.〕

Because expenditure cannot be met and the fiscal administration reports an empty treasury, you gentlemen ask us students to probe the abuses to their source and set forth measures that can endure. This is a major concern of the state, one for which the court has diligently sought a solution day and night for far more than a single day. Previously, the crafty northern enemy watched for lapses in the frontier officials' vigilance and burst into the outskirts of our capital, causing great alarm at court and throughout the realm. Thereupon, those holding military command [?] pleaded that their strength was unequal to the enemy's. They summoned skilled fighting men from the various frontiers to defend the capital and also recruited able and courageous men widely as new troops, increasing annual expenditure by hundreds of thousands.

Even before this, because beacon alarms arose unpredictably along the frontiers, the benefits of military agricultural colonies and the salt system had been lost. Unable to supply themselves, frontier authorities repeatedly sought assistance from the palace treasury, and state finances were already suffering. Attempts to reduce expenditure had failed; now it expanded still further, bringing severe distress. Fiscal officials and advisers sought to devise lasting measures for the state, gathering to deliberate and planning with counting rods in hand. Whether in the grand plans and detailed proposals formulated at court or in the institutions established and reforms undertaken outside it, they eliminated superfluous personnel, curtailed unnecessary expenditure, expanded opportunities to obtain privileges through contributions, collected monetary payments for redemption of penalties, and pressed for payment of arrears. Down to such minor items as postal relay services and calendar paper, nothing escaped monetary assessment and remittance to the central treasury. Their efforts could be called exhaustive. Yet revenue ultimately did not…

title: 隆慶元年順天府鄉試錄
text:
當所出特以應目前急者先歲羨餘耳今
則帑蓄既竭雖欲為目前計將不可得此
固執事者之所不能釋慮與且匹夫而有
千金之產則必計租田緡息所收為俯仰
衣食奉務使所入常贏則雖有意外之虞
非時之費不為所困矣其次計歲所收以
為費而無餘居常亦足以自支不可以待
變又其下入廉而費侈則產必日耗矣蓋
蘇子謂為國有三計王制所稱三十年之
===
通制國用可以九年無饑歲入足用而有
餘九年之蓄常閒而無用者萬世之計也
一歲天下之產僅供一歲之用一時之計
也量出以為入用之不給取之益多天下
晏然而盡用衰世苟且之法不終月之計
也夫以天下之大九州之富而至為不終
月之計豈謀國者之長算哉然而萬世之
計不可以歲月建也而經用則不一日不
可缺者是以自虜犯近圻以來謀國者□

當所出恃以應目前急者先歲羨餘耳今
則帑藏既竭雖欲爲目前計將不可得此
固執事者之所不能釋慮與且匹夫而有
千金之産則必計租田稽息所收爲俯仰
衣食奉務使所入常贏則雖有意外之虞

爲費而無餘居常亦足以自支不可以待
變又其下入廉而費侈則産必日耗矣蓋
蘇子謂爲國有三計王制所稱三十年之
通制國用可以九年無饑歲入足用而有
餘九年之蓄常閒而無用者萬世之計也
===
一歲天下之産僅供一歲之用一時之計
也量出以爲入用之不給取之益多天下
晏然而盡用衆世苟且之法不終月之計
也夫以天下之大九州之富而至爲不終
月之計豈謀國者之長算哉然而萬世之
計不可以歲月建也而經用則有一日不
可缺者是以自腐犯近圻以來□□□□
punctuated:
當所出，特以應目前急者，先歲羨餘耳。今則帑蓄既竭，雖欲為目前計，將不可得。此固執事者之所不能釋慮與！且匹夫而有千金之產，則必計租田緡息所收，為俯仰衣食奉，務使所入常贏，則雖有意外之虞、非時之費，不為所困矣。其次，計歲所收以為費而無餘，居常亦足以自支，不可以待變。又其下，入廉而費侈，則產必日耗矣。
蓋蘇子謂為國有三計：王制所稱「三十年之通，制國用，可以九年無饑」，歲入足用而有餘，九年之蓄常閒而無用者，萬世之計也。一歲天下之產，僅供一歲之用，一時之計也。量出以為入，用之不給，取之益多，天下晏然而盡用，衰世苟且之法，不終月之計也。夫以天下之大、九州之富，而至為不終月之計，豈謀國者之長算哉？然而萬世之計，不可以歲月建也，而經用則不一日不可缺者。是以自虜犯近圻以來，謀國者□
translation_en:
…match expenditures; what has served to meet the immediate emergency has merely been the surpluses of previous years. Now that the treasury’s reserves are exhausted, even devising a plan for present needs will be impossible. Surely this is something those in charge cannot cease worrying about!
Consider an ordinary man with property worth a thousand pieces of gold. He must calculate his receipts from land rents and interest on money to provide clothing and food for himself and his dependents, taking care that his income always leaves a surplus. Then, even if unforeseen troubles or untimely expenses arise, they will not put him in difficulty. The next best course is to base expenditures on annual receipts, leaving no surplus: this suffices to sustain him in ordinary times but cannot prepare him for unexpected change. Worse still, if income is small and spending extravagant, his property must dwindle daily.
Master Su said that there are three kinds of fiscal planning for a state. As the Royal Regulations puts it, “Taking a comprehensive reckoning over thirty years to regulate state expenditure, one can withstand nine years without famine.” When annual revenue meets expenses and leaves a surplus, while reserves sufficient for nine years remain constantly untouched and unused, this is planning for ten thousand generations. When the whole realm’s annual production barely supplies its annual needs, this is planning for the moment. When revenue is determined by expenditure, and ever more is extracted as spending outstrips resources, so that everything is consumed even while the realm is at peace, this is the expedient method of a declining age—planning that will not last out a month. With a realm so vast and the wealth of the Nine Provinces, to descend to planning that will not last out a month—can this be the far-sighted calculation of those who devise policy for the state?
Yet a plan for ten thousand generations cannot be established within a few months or years, while ordinary expenditures cannot go unmet for even a single day. Thus, ever since the northern invaders encroached upon the environs of the capital, those who devise policy for the state [illegible] …

title: 隆慶元年順天府鄉試錄
text:
常三致意矣而議論滋多經制卒不能以
時定夫豈不遠觀詳度為
國家深長思哉目前之急無計以紓之而欲
徵效數年之外固不能待也然則當今之
計必何如而後可耶夫醫師之攻疾急則
治標緩則治本非其本之可後也救急當
然耳標證去則本可得而理矣今度支之
經費不啻急矣欲以紓目前則不可無治
標之方欲以謀久遠則不可不求治本之
===
要規制定則財用可以次第而理矣夫所
謂治標者何也血氣之不調也邪攻之財
用之不節也弊蠹之審受病之因然後治
療之術不悖未有不得其因而善其治者
也財用之在天下有生出之原有制用之
節失其原當求所以生之失其節當求所
以制之今天下財賦自漕運外其以銀輸
大倉庫領於度支之經費者歲入一百一
十六萬有奇而各轉運司餘鹽課銀一百
alt_text:
窮三致意矣而議論滋多經制卒不能以
時定夫豈不遠觀詳度爲
國家深長思哉目前之急無計以紓之而欲
徼效數年之外固不能待也然則當今之
計必何如而後可耶夫醫師之攻疾急則
治標緩則治本非其本之可後也救急當
然耳標證去則本可得而理矣今度支之
經費不啻急矣欲以紓目前則不可無治
標之方欲以謀久遠則不可不求治本之
===
要規制定則財用可以次第而理矣夫所
謂治標者何也血氣之不調也邪攻之財
用之不節也弊竇之當受病之因然後治
療之術不悖未有不得其因而善其治者
也財用之在天下有生出之原有制用之
節失其原當求所以生之失其節當求所
以制之今天下財賦自漕運外其以銀輸
大倉庫領於度支之經費者歲入一百一
十六萬有奇而各轉運司餘鹽課銀一百
punctuated:
常三致意矣，而議論滋多，經制卒不能以時定。夫豈不遠觀詳度，為國家深長思哉？目前之急，無計以紓之，而欲徵效數年之外，固不能待也。然則當今之計，必何如而後可耶？夫醫師之攻疾，急則治標，緩則治本，非其本之可後也，救急當然耳。標證去，則本可得而理矣。今度支之經費不啻急矣，欲以紓目前，則不可無治標之方；欲以謀久遠，則不可不求治本之要。規制定，則財用可以次第而理矣。
夫所謂治標者何也？血氣之不調也，邪攻之；財用之不節也，弊蠹之。審受病之因，然後治療之術不悖，未有不得其因而善其治者也。財用之在天下，有生出之原，有制用之節。失其原，當求所以生之；失其節，當求所以制之。
今天下財賦，自漕運外，其以銀輸大倉庫、領於度支之經費者，歲入一百一十六萬有奇，而各轉運司餘鹽課銀一百
translation_en:
…have repeatedly given the matter their attention. Yet discussions have multiplied, and the fiscal arrangements have ultimately failed to be settled in time. Surely this is not because they have failed to look far ahead, weigh matters carefully, and think deeply about the state's long-term interests? But with no means of relieving the immediate crisis, they seek results several years hence: there is simply no time to wait. What, then, must the present plan be if it is to prove workable? When physicians attack an illness, they treat its manifestations in an emergency and its root when circumstances permit. This is not because the root can be neglected; it is simply what emergency relief requires. Once the manifestations have been removed, the root can be treated. The funding of regular state expenditure is now more than urgent. To relieve the immediate crisis, we must have a method for treating the manifestations; to plan for the distant future, we must also seek the essentials of treating the root. Once regulations are established, state finances can be put in order step by step.
What is meant by treating the manifestations? When blood and vital energy are out of balance, harmful influences are attacking them; when fiscal expenditure lacks restraint, abuses are eating away at it. Only after examining the cause of the illness can the treatment avoid going astray. No one has ever treated an illness well without discovering its cause. Throughout the realm, fiscal resources have sources from which they are generated and rules governing their expenditure. If their sources are lost, we must seek ways to generate them; if restraint is lost, we must seek ways to regulate their use.
At present, apart from grain transported by canal, the realm's tax revenues remitted in silver to the Dacang Treasury [?] and administered for regular state expenditure amount annually to more than 1,160,000 taels. The surplus salt-tax silver from the various Salt Distribution Commissions amounts to one hundred…

title: 隆慶元年順天府鄉試錄
text:
三萬有竒數止此矣九邊主客兵餽餉嵗
為銀二百三十六萬有竒
內府之供應官員之俸給京衞兵馬之布花
芻菽嵗為銀一百三十五萬有竒一嵗所
出浮於入數一百五十餘萬而一切取民
之道亦既搜括詳盡不可復加矣治標之
術惟有節其流已耳節之何如曰
上供所須固不可缺矣宮府一體其諸監局
之濫役無名之冒破可革也官員俸給固
不可缺矣職以事列額外之剩員錦衣之
帶俸可汰也芻菽嵗供固不可缺矣而主
守之侵冒奸詭之虛出可覈也
聖天子躬履節儉諸秕政冗役裁停畧盡誠於
是三者斷而行之其所省當不啻十之五
矣然其費鉅而用急者又特在邊餉夫舉
天下嵗入以供邊不敷十一故邊餉當議
九邊嵗餉二百三十餘萬而宣大薊鎮居
其三之二故三鎮尤當議三鎮嵗餉一百
alt_text:
三萬有竒數止此矣九邊主客兵餽餉歲
爲銀二百三十六萬有竒
內府之供應官員之俸給京衛兵馬之布花
芻菽歲爲銀一百三十五萬有竒一歲所
出浮於入數一百五十餘萬而一切取民
之道亦旣搜括詳盡不可復加矣治標之
術惟有節其流已耳節之何如曰
上供所須固不可缺矣宮府一體其諸監局
之濫役無名之冒破可革也官員俸給固
===
不可缺矣職以事列額外之剩員錦衣之
帶俸可汰也芻菽歲供固不可缺矣而主
守之侵冒奸詭之虛出可覈也
聖天子躬履節儉諸秕政冗役裁停畧盡誠於
是三者斷而行之其所省當不啻十之五
矣然其費鉅而用急者又特在邊餉夫舉
天下歲入以供邊不敷十一故邊餉當議
九邊歲餉二百三十餘萬而宣大薊鎮居
其三之二故三鎮尤當議三鎮歲餉一百
punctuated:
三萬有竒，數止此矣。九邊主客兵餽餉，嵗為銀二百三十六萬有竒；內府之供應、官員之俸給、京衞兵馬之布花芻菽，嵗為銀一百三十五萬有竒。一嵗所出浮於入數一百五十餘萬，而一切取民之道亦既搜括詳盡，不可復加矣。治標之術，惟有節其流已耳。節之何如？曰：上供所須，固不可缺矣；宮府一體，其諸監局之濫役、無名之冒破，可革也。官員俸給，固不可缺矣；職以事列，額外之剩員、錦衣之帶俸，可汰也。芻菽嵗供，固不可缺矣；而主守之侵冒、奸詭之虛出，可覈也。聖天子躬履節儉，諸秕政冗役裁停畧盡，誠於是三者斷而行之，其所省當不啻十之五矣。
然其費鉅而用急者，又特在邊餉。夫舉天下嵗入以供邊，不敷十一，故邊餉當議。九邊嵗餉二百三十餘萬，而宣、大、薊鎮居其三之二，故三鎮尤當議。三鎮嵗餉一百
translation_en:
…1,030,000 taels and more: the revenues amount to no more than this. Provisions and pay for the resident and guest troops of the Nine Frontier Commands cost over 2,360,000 taels of silver annually. Supplies for the inner palace, officials’ salaries, and cloth, cotton, fodder, and beans for the troops and horses of the capital guards cost over 1,350,000 taels annually. Annual expenditure exceeds revenue by more than 1,500,000 taels. Every means of exacting resources from the people has already been exhaustively pursued; nothing more can be added. The only remedy for these symptoms is to restrain the outflow.
How is it to be restrained? I answer: supplies required for the throne certainly cannot be withheld. Yet the palace and the government form a single body: excessive employment in the various palace directorates and bureaus, and fraudulent expenditures without legitimate grounds, can be abolished. Officials’ salaries certainly cannot be withheld. Yet offices are established according to their duties: surplus officials beyond the authorized complement and those drawing salaries without substantive duties in the Embroidered-uniform Guard can be eliminated. Annual supplies of fodder and beans certainly cannot be withheld. Yet embezzlement and fraudulent claims by their custodians, and fictitious disbursements contrived through deception, can be investigated. Our sage Son of Heaven personally practices frugality and has already abolished nearly all defective administrative practices and unnecessary services. If these three measures were resolutely implemented, the savings would surely amount to more than half.
Nevertheless, the greatest expense and most urgent demand lie particularly in frontier military provisions. Even if the entire realm’s annual revenue were devoted to the frontier, it would fall short by a tenth. Frontier provisioning therefore requires deliberation. Annual provisions for the Nine Frontier Commands cost more than 2,300,000 taels, and the commands of Xuanfu, Datong, and Jizhou account for two-thirds of this. These three commands therefore require particular deliberation. Annual provisions for the three commands amount to one million …

title: 隆慶元年順天府鄉試錄
text:
五十餘萬而薊居其二之一故薊鎮尤當
議夫發内帑濟邊蓋昉於正統丁卯於時
運遼東銀十萬宣大十五萬耳正德間王
文恪建議已謂
國家邊費最大歲用銀至四五十萬欲以省
之矣而豈知今日之至此極耶蓋宣大歲
額之增在嘉靖辛丑壬寅時薊鎮則以庚
戌始皆以黠虜匪茹創巨痛深思一振厲
興起之故不惜經費為促辦計迨後遂沿
以為常饋輸稍後時則邊臣執左劵索負
故以天下之力困於此三鎮耳夫以周之
盛而獫狁侵鎬及方以唐太宗之威略而
突厥内訌至便橋始退中國與北狄鄰時
遭其侵掠常爾往者中國習於久安忽覩
狂虜颸發遠邇惴懾若毒蛟猛獸不可嚮
禦帥閫不逞之臣因張聲勢内竭厚集廣
募徼倖一旦無事遂使延固遼左萬里之
兵疲於奔命内帑數世之積罄於轉輸厲

興起之故不惜經費爲從辦計追後邊沿
===

故以天下之力困於此三鎮耳夫以周之
盛而玁狁侵鎬及方以唐太宗之威略而

遭其侵掠常爾往者中國習於久安忽報
狂虜飈發遠邇惴懾若毒蛟猛獸不可嚮

punctuated:
五十餘萬，而薊居其二之一，故薊鎮尤當議。夫發内帑濟邊，蓋昉於正統丁卯，於時運遼東銀十萬、宣大十五萬耳。正德間，王文恪建議，已謂國家邊費最大，歲用銀至四五十萬，欲以省之矣，而豈知今日之至此極耶？蓋宣大歲額之增，在嘉靖辛丑、壬寅時；薊鎮則以庚戌始。皆以黠虜匪茹，創巨痛深，思一振厲興起之故，不惜經費，為促辦計。迨後遂沿以為常，饋輸稍後時，則邊臣執左劵索負，故以天下之力困於此三鎮耳。
夫以周之盛，而獫狁侵鎬及方；以唐太宗之威略，而突厥内訌，至便橋始退。中國與北狄鄰，時遭其侵掠，常爾。往者中國習於久安，忽覩狂虜颸發，遠邇惴懾，若毒蛟猛獸，不可嚮禦。帥閫不逞之臣，因張聲勢，内竭厚集，廣募徼倖。一旦無事，遂使延固遼左萬里之兵疲於奔命，内帑數世之積罄於轉輸。厲
translation_en:
…more than 1.5 million, of which Ji accounts for half; thus the Ji garrison especially warrants deliberation. Disbursing funds from the imperial treasury to assist the frontier began in the dingmao year of Zhengtong [1447]. At that time, only 100,000 taels of silver were sent to Liaodong and 150,000 to Xuanfu and Datong. During the Zhengde reign, Wang Wenke submitted a proposal already stating that the state's frontier expenditures were its greatest expense, with annual silver outlays reaching 400,000 or 500,000 taels, and sought to reduce them. How could he have known that matters would reach today's extreme? The increases in the annual allocations for Xuanfu and Datong occurred in the xinchou and renyin years of Jiajing [1541 and 1542]; those for the Ji garrison began in the gengxu year [1550]. In every case, the cunning enemy's implacability had inflicted grievous wounds and deep suffering, prompting a desire to rouse our strength and take action. Consequently, no expense was spared in arranging matters with all speed. Thereafter, these allocations continued as established practice. Whenever supplies arrived even slightly late, frontier officials demanded the arrears like creditors holding the left-hand halves of contracts. Thus the resources of the entire realm have been exhausted by these three garrisons alone.
Even at the height of Zhou's power, the Xianyun invaded Hao and Fang; even with Emperor Taizong of Tang's military might and strategic skill, the Turks stirred up turmoil within the realm and withdrew only after reaching Bian Bridge. As the Central Realm borders the northern barbarians, occasional incursions and plundering are commonplace. Formerly, after becoming accustomed to prolonged peace, the Central Realm suddenly witnessed the frenzied enemy erupting like a gust of wind [?]. Near and far, people trembled in fear, as though confronted by venomous dragons or fierce beasts that could not be faced and resisted. Unscrupulous officials in military commands took advantage of this to magnify the alarm, draining resources within the realm and amassing great quantities of supplies [?], recruiting widely, and hoping for a lucky outcome. Once matters became quiet, the result was that troops from Yansui, Guyuan, and Liaodong, across ten thousand li, had been exhausted by rushing to answer summons, while the imperial treasury's reserves accumulated over several reigns had been emptied by transport and provisioning. Calamity…

title: 隆慶元年順天府鄉試錄
text:
階爲梗至貽今日不可支之憂而猶不思
所以變通將安所稅駕耶夫虜雖無歲不
犯中國然每犯必易其地自庚戌犯薊以
來率數歲而一至而我之調遣征發恐恐
然常若虜至者則終歲無閑時此以主爲
客變逸爲勞術也兵家之所禁也矧始之
徵調客兵以士兵未練耳朞月可責效者
無已則如孔子所謂七年即戎乎今且二
十年而客兵之入衞者猶昔則所謂練兵
===
者豈皆虛言耶夫使封疆之臣不以實心
狥
國家之急豈惟士兵難恃將雖厚集客兵亦
且無益即徃事可睹明效矣今欲爲經久
計則務在破拘攣之見信必至之畫而求
可成之功凡諸遠鎮客兵盡罷不徵而令
近鎮選集武勇屯境上待命凡虜大舉非
飄忽而至也蓋必有先聲焉聞警宣大兵
自紫荆居庸入遼東兵自山海入必不後

punctuated:
階爲梗，至貽今日不可支之憂，而猶不思所以變通，將安所稅駕耶？夫虜雖無歲不犯中國，然每犯必易其地。自庚戌犯薊以來，率數歲而一至，而我之調遣征發，恐恐然常若虜至者，則終歲無閑時。此以主爲客、變逸爲勞術也，兵家之所禁也。矧始之徵調客兵，以士兵未練耳。朞月可責效者，無已則如孔子所謂七年即戎乎？今且二十年，而客兵之入衞者猶昔，則所謂練兵者，豈皆虛言耶？夫使封疆之臣不以實心狥國家之急，豈惟士兵難恃，將雖厚集客兵，亦且無益，即徃事可睹明效矣。
今欲爲經久計，則務在破拘攣之見，信必至之畫，而求可成之功。凡諸遠鎮客兵，盡罷不徵，而令近鎮選集武勇，屯境上待命。凡虜大舉，非飄忽而至也，蓋必有先聲焉。聞警，宣大兵自紫荆、居庸入，遼東兵自山海入，必不後
translation_en:
…became a source of trouble, leaving us with today’s unsustainable predicament. Yet we still give no thought to adapting our methods. Where, then, can we ever bring matters to rest? Although the enemy invades China every year, each invasion strikes a different place. Since the invasion of Ji in the gengxu year [1550], they have generally come there only once every few years. Yet our troop deployments and mobilizations continue in constant alarm, as though the enemy were always arriving, leaving no respite throughout the year. This is a method of turning the defending host into a visiting army and ease into exhaustion—something military strategists forbid. Moreover, troops from other garrisons were initially called up only because our soldiers were untrained. Results could have been demanded within a full year; at the very most, should it not have been as Confucius said, that after seven years they could take up arms? Now nearly twenty years have passed, and troops from elsewhere still come to defend us just as before. Can all this talk of training troops have been empty words? If officials responsible for the frontiers do not sincerely devote themselves to the state’s urgent needs, it is not merely our soldiers who will prove unreliable: even assembling large numbers of troops from elsewhere will be useless. Past events already provide clear evidence of this.
If we now wish to make lasting plans, we must break free of constricted views, put our trust in plans that can assuredly be carried through, and seek attainable results. All call-ups of troops from distant frontier garrisons should cease. Nearby garrisons should instead be ordered to select and assemble brave fighting men and station them along the border to await orders. A major enemy invasion does not materialize in an instant; there will surely be advance indications. Upon receiving an alarm, troops from Xuanfu and Datong can enter through Zijing and Juyong passes, and troops from Liaodong through Shanhai Pass. They will certainly not arrive later …

title: 隆慶元年順天府鄉試錄
text:
虜矣要在間諜明而傳召速耳矧漁陽突
騎古稱雄鷙果練習有方亦何至全恃客
兵者如此則司農費必大省況歲額之增
或以資召募或以備械器或以供興事不
常之用司農按籍而覈之諸勿使麗於額
焉至於修邊之費既告成績矣即每歲不
無補緝要於始事有間亦須定為制額歲
循為度推而之宣大亦然覈其歲額之所
增而汰其費之尤無經者又推而之各邊
===
亦然覈其歲額之所增而汰其費之尤無
經者則歲入雖無贏當必不窘於應矣目
前之急既紓又當立經制以圖久遠蓋標
證既除復須理其本耳治本亦豈有異道
乎不過復
國初各邊所以自贍之法耳法安在曰屯田
曰鹽法此二策者夫孰不言之而卒不能
立者非其法之果難行行之者不得其方
耳夫法惟宜於人情斯法立而可久而修

兵者如此則司農費必大省況歲額之增
或以資召募或以備械器或以供興事不
常之用司農按籍而覈之諸勿使罷於額
馬至於修邊之費既告成績矣即每歲不
無補緝要於始事有間亦須定爲常額歲
循爲度推而之宣大亦然覈其歲額之所
增而汰其費之尤無經者又推而之各邊
===
亦然覈其歲額之所增而汰其費之尤無
經者則歲入雖無贏當必不窘於應矣目
前之急既紓又當立經制以圖久遠蓋標
證既除復須理其本耳治本亦豈有異道
乎不過復
國初各邊所以自贍之法耳法安在曰屯田
曰鹽法此二策者夫孰不言之而卒不能
立者非其法之果難行行之者不得其方
耳夫法惟宜於人情斯法立而可久而後
punctuated:
虜矣。要在間諜明而傳召速耳。矧漁陽突騎，古稱雄鷙，果練習有方，亦何至全恃客兵者？如此，則司農費必大省。況歲額之增，或以資召募，或以備械器，或以供興事不常之用，司農按籍而覈之，諸勿使麗於額焉。至於修邊之費，既告成績矣，即每歲不無補緝，要於始事有間，亦須定為制額，歲循為度。推而之宣大亦然，覈其歲額之所增，而汰其費之尤無經者。又推而之各邊亦然，覈其歲額之所增，而汰其費之尤無經者。則歲入雖無贏，當必不窘於應矣。
目前之急既紓，又當立經制以圖久遠。蓋標證既除，復須理其本耳。治本亦豈有異道乎？不過復國初各邊所以自贍之法耳。法安在？曰屯田，曰鹽法。此二策者，夫孰不言之？而卒不能立者，非其法之果難行，行之者不得其方耳。夫法惟宜於人情，斯法立而可久，而修
translation_en:
…the enemy. What matters is simply that intelligence be accurate and summonses transmitted swiftly. Moreover, the assault cavalry of Yuyang have been renowned since antiquity for their valor and ferocity. If they are properly trained, why should there be any need to rely entirely on troops brought in from elsewhere? In this way, expenditure by the Minister of Revenue would certainly be greatly reduced. Furthermore, increases in annual allocations may fund recruitment, provide weapons and equipment, or meet extraordinary expenses arising from undertakings. The Minister of Revenue should examine these against the registers and ensure that none are incorporated into the regular allocation. As for expenditure on repairing the frontier defenses, the work has already been reported complete. Although some repairs will inevitably be needed each year, their cost should differ from that of the initial undertaking. A statutory allocation must therefore be fixed, to serve as the annual limit. The same procedure should be extended to Xuanfu and Datong: investigate increases in their annual allocations and eliminate expenditures that are especially lacking in established justification. Extend this procedure to all the other frontier regions as well: investigate increases in their annual allocations and eliminate expenditures that are especially lacking in established justification. Then, even if annual revenues yield no surplus, there should certainly be no difficulty in meeting expenses.
Once the immediate emergency has been relieved, permanent regulations should also be established with the long term in view. For once the outward symptoms have been removed, the root must still be treated. Is there some different way to treat the root? It requires only restoring the methods by which the frontier regions supported themselves at the beginning of the dynasty. What are these methods? Agricultural colonies and the salt system. Who does not speak of these two policies? Their ultimate failure to become established is not because they are truly difficult to implement, but because those implementing them have not found the proper approach. Only when a system accords with human inclinations can it become established and endure; and in restoring…

title: 隆慶元年順天府鄉試錄
text:
復久廢之政者又貴不泥其迹各邊自邇
年武事不競居民益稀有可溝洫播殖之
地而鞠為榛莽者彌望也軍民非不欲得
而田之然畏虜之蹂躪不敢今誠相度地
勢為封畛砦壁使之遠近聯絡足以相倚
助募民任力穡者賦田一區蠲其租入三
年而後收之輕其課與民田比則人必樂
從人樂從則塞下之粟必多粟多則官必
收其利矣此與清原屯之田先構怨嫌按
===
籍而授之屯卒以彊其力作者不可同日
語矣至於鹽法之斁則由昔之見小利者
為重估以困商而餘鹽之開納於運司者
又安坐而享厚利自是商之挾厚貲者不
復出塞不惟飛輓利失而邊民衣食之具
仰給於中國者益窘於求故內帑之鏹愈
出而邊塞愈急者率數金不獲一金用耳
屯田既復本色且易得又輕其估以召之
利之所在宜必有應者俟法漸疏暢併以

punctuated:
復久廢之政者，又貴不泥其迹。各邊自邇年武事不競，居民益稀，有可溝洫播殖之地，而鞠為榛莽者彌望也。軍民非不欲得而田之，然畏虜之蹂躪，不敢。今誠相度地勢，為封畛砦壁，使之遠近聯絡，足以相倚助；募民任力穡者，賦田一區，蠲其租入三年而後收之，輕其課，與民田比，則人必樂從。人樂從，則塞下之粟必多；粟多，則官必收其利矣。此與清原屯之田，先構怨嫌，按籍而授之屯卒，以彊其力作者，不可同日語矣。
至於鹽法之斁，則由昔之見小利者，為重估以困商，而餘鹽之開納於運司者，又安坐而享厚利。自是商之挾厚貲者，不復出塞，不惟飛輓利失，而邊民衣食之具仰給於中國者，益窘於求。故內帑之鏹愈出，而邊塞愈急者，率數金不獲一金用耳。屯田既復，本色且易得，又輕其估以召之，利之所在，宜必有應者。俟法漸疏暢，併以
translation_en:
…in restoring institutions long fallen into disuse, it is also essential not to cling rigidly to their former forms. In recent years, military weakness along the frontiers has left the population increasingly sparse. Land suitable for irrigation channels and cultivation lies abandoned to thickets as far as the eye can see. Soldiers and civilians would gladly obtain and cultivate it, but fear of devastation by the raiders keeps them from daring to do so. If we now carefully survey the terrain and establish field boundaries and fortified stockades, linking nearby and distant sites so that they can support one another, we can recruit civilians willing to undertake agricultural labor and allot each a tract of land. Exempt them from rent payments for three years before beginning collection, and keep their assessments light, on a par with those on civilian farmland. People will then gladly participate. With willing participation, grain along the frontier will certainly become plentiful; with plentiful grain, the government will certainly reap the benefit. This cannot be compared with reclaiming the original military agricultural colony lands—thereby provoking resentment at the outset—and allotting them to colony soldiers according to the registers, compelling them to cultivate them.
As for the deterioration of the salt system, this arose because those who previously sought petty gains imposed high valuations that burdened merchants, while those making payments for surplus salt at the Salt Distribution Commission could sit comfortably and enjoy substantial profits. Thereafter, merchants with ample capital no longer ventured beyond the passes. Not only were the benefits of grain transport lost, but frontier inhabitants also found it increasingly difficult to obtain the necessities of food and clothing that they depended on the interior to supply. Thus ever more silver left the imperial treasury, while frontier needs grew ever more urgent: several units of silver generally failed to yield even one unit’s worth of use. Once the military agricultural colonies are restored, grain payments in kind will become easier to obtain. If salt valuations are also lowered to attract merchants, the prospect of profit should certainly draw a response. Once the system gradually operates more smoothly, also use…

title: 隆慶元年順天府鄉試錄
text:
餘鹽闢之邊令引納倍粟運司給鹽如之
使商不由邊開中者無所牟利則益爭赴
塞下商通則百貨集邊人益有所取饒而
仰於内者輕則内帑之財益可以省出而
嵗有餘嵗嵗而積之則王制所謂九年之
蓄漢文景粟陳貫朽之盛可馴致矣此固
萬世之計所謂良醫之治本者也執事念
財用之急俾諸生勿勦陳說欲聞至計而
愚生之所復者卒莫能竒蓋揆之時勢酌
===
之情法不過如此若夫桑孔牢盆均輸之
法王安石呂惠卿青苗免役之令廼市賈
之魁駔儈之術耳縉紳先生羞稱之亦何
暇摧其利病而較其短長哉

仰於內者輕則內帑之財益可以省出而
歲有餘歲歲而積之則王制所謂九年之
蓄漢文景粟陳貫朽之盛可馴致矣此固
萬世之計所謂良醫之治本者也執事念
財用之急俾諸生勿勦陳說欲聞至計而
愚生之所復者卒莫能奇蓋揆之時勢酌
===
之情法不過如此若夫桑孔牢盆均輸之
法王安石呂惠卿青苗免役之令迺市賈
之黠駔儈之術拜縛絣先生羞稱之亦何
暇摧其利病而較其短長哉
punctuated: 餘鹽闢之邊，令引納倍粟，運司給鹽如之。使商不由邊開中者無所牟利，則益爭赴塞下。商通則百貨集，邊人益有所取饒，而仰於内者輕，則内帑之財益可以省出而嵗有餘。嵗嵗而積之，則《王制》所謂九年之蓄、漢文景粟陳貫朽之盛，可馴致矣。此固萬世之計，所謂良醫之治本者也。執事念財用之急，俾諸生勿勦陳說，欲聞至計，而愚生之所復者卒莫能竒。蓋揆之時勢，酌之情法，不過如此。若夫桑孔牢盆、均輸之法，王安石、呂惠卿青苗、免役之令，廼市賈之魁、駔儈之術耳。縉紳先生羞稱之，亦何暇摧其利病而較其短長哉？
translation_en:
…extend the arrangements for surplus salt to the frontier as well, requiring merchants to deliver twice the amount of grain per salt certificate, with the Salt Distribution Commission issuing salt in the corresponding amount. If merchants cannot make a profit without obtaining salt entitlements through grain deliveries at the frontier, they will compete all the more eagerly to go there. When merchant traffic flows freely, all kinds of goods will gather, and frontier inhabitants will have more abundant supplies to draw upon. Their dependence on the interior will diminish, allowing further reductions in expenditure from the palace treasury and leaving a surplus each year. With accumulation year after year, the nine years’ reserves spoken of in “Royal Regulations,” and the prosperity of the reigns of Emperors Wen and Jing of the Han—when grain grew old in storage and the strings holding cash rotted away—can gradually be attained. This is indeed a plan for all ages: what is meant by a good physician treating the root of an illness.

You, sir, mindful of the urgency of financial needs, have instructed us students not to plagiarize stale arguments, wishing to hear the best possible proposals. Yet what this humble student has offered in reply has, in the end, nothing remarkable about it. For, weighing present circumstances and considering practical conditions and established rules, the course to take amounts to no more than this. As for Sang and Kong’s salt-boiling monopoly and equitable transport measures, or Wang Anshi and Lü Huiqing’s Green Sprouts loans and service-exemption ordinances, these are merely the techniques of master traders and brokers. Gentlemen of official standing are ashamed even to mention them; what leisure have they, then, to examine [?] their benefits and harms or compare their strengths and weaknesses?

皇上膺曆紀元之秋天下當復賓
興士于鄉臣士美臣四維奉
欽命典順天府試事事竣錄成
臣四維謹申言于末簡曰自
古治道隆汚徵諸人材而人
材盛衰關乎士習士習不可
===
不慎也先王知其然乃設庠
序以教于鄉建頖宮辟雝以
教於國陳其德行道藝之目
立爲訓迪庸威之節以明示
好惡俾士童而習焉長而安
焉不見異物而遷焉是以化
行俗美賢才衆而邦家昌也

皇上膺曆紀元之秋，天下當復賓興士于鄉。臣士美、臣四維奉欽命典順天府試事。事竣，錄成，臣四維謹申言于末簡曰：自古治道隆汚，徵諸人材，而人材盛衰，關乎士習。士習不可不慎也。先王知其然，乃設庠序以教于鄉，建頖宮、辟雝以教於國，陳其德行道藝之目，立爲訓迪庸威之節，以明示好惡，俾士童而習焉，長而安焉，不見異物而遷焉。是以化行俗美，賢才衆而邦家昌也。
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination

In the autumn when His Majesty received the imperial succession and inaugurated his reign era, it was time once again throughout the realm to honor and select scholars through the provincial examinations. Your servants Shimei and Siwei received the imperial command to preside over the examination in Shuntian Prefecture. With the proceedings concluded and the record completed, your servant Siwei respectfully adds these words on its final pages:

Since antiquity, the flourishing or decline of governance has been evident in the men of talent it possesses, while the abundance or scarcity of talent depends upon the habits of scholars. These habits must therefore receive careful attention. Knowing this, the former kings established local schools to teach in the rural communities, and built the Pangong and Biyong academies to teach in the capitals of the states and the royal realm. They set forth the subjects of virtue, conduct, principles, and arts, and established rules for instruction, guidance, employment, and punishment, thereby clearly showing what they approved and disapproved. Thus scholars practiced these teachings in childhood and became at ease with them as adults, without being diverted upon encountering unfamiliar things. Consequently, moral transformation spread, customs became good, worthy and talented men abounded, and the state prospered.

title: 隆慶元年順天府鄉試錄
text:
我
太祖皇帝經始鴻業方擐甲四征
即建大學京師崇首善迨即
位二年而天下之郡縣有學
矣八年而天下郡縣之鄉社
有學矣其教士一以孔氏之
道六經之文而訓義一以程
朱為正其制舉一以經義論
策而詞賦雜科不與焉蓋自
成周而後道術純白品式詳
備無如我
朝者昔漢承秦滅學之餘師異
教人異習董仲舒啓武帝表
章六經尊信孔子而漢儒經

我太祖皇帝經始鴻業，方擐甲四征，即建大學京師，崇首善。迨即位二年，而天下之郡縣有學矣；八年，而天下郡縣之鄉社有學矣。其教士，一以孔氏之道、六經之文，而訓義一以程朱為正；其制舉，一以經義、論、策，而詞賦雜科不與焉。蓋自成周而後，道術純白，品式詳備，無如我朝者。
昔漢承秦滅學之餘，師異教，人異習。董仲舒啓武帝表章六經，尊信孔子，而漢儒經
translation_en:
When our Emperor Taizu laid the foundations of his great enterprise, while still clad in armor and campaigning in all directions, he established the Imperial University in the capital to exalt it as the foremost exemplar of goodness. By the second year after his accession, prefectures and counties throughout the realm had schools; by the eighth year, the rural communities of those prefectures and counties also had schools. In educating scholars, he relied exclusively on the Way of Confucius and the writings of the Six Classics, taking the interpretations of Cheng and Zhu alone as authoritative. The examinations he instituted employed only essays on the meaning of the Classics, discourses, and policy essays; verse, rhapsodies, and miscellaneous examination categories had no place in them. Indeed, since the flourishing Zhou dynasty, no dynasty has equaled ours in the purity of its teachings and the comprehensiveness of its regulations.
Formerly, the Han inherited the aftermath of the Qin destruction of learning: teachers differed in what they taught, and individuals differed in what they studied. Dong Zhongshu urged Emperor Wu to give prominence to the Six Classics and to revere and trust Confucius, and the Han scholars’ interpretations of the Classics…

translation_en:
…interpretations thus gained renown in the world. Yet their specialized traditions, handed down through generations, although shedding considerable light on the Way of the sages, could not comprehensively penetrate its fundamental sources or fully expound its meanings and categories. The Tang again exalted literary composition, further obstructing the path to the Classics. Only when the Cheng brothers, Zhu Xi, and other Confucian scholars emerged in the Song did the Way of Confucius shine forth clearly. Yet the rulers of the age again failed to follow this path in establishing schools and cultivating scholars. Such is the difficulty of illuminating the Way and correcting entrenched practices!
Today, scholars are fortunate to live in an age of cultural enlightenment and to receive the instruction of the imperial Supreme Standard. From childhood, when they attend local schools, until adulthood, what meets their eyes or sounds in their ears is invariably the teaching of Confucius and the interpretations of the Cheng brothers and Zhu Xi. Thus, in the present age [?], in elaborating benevolence and righteousness, distinguishing kingly rule from hegemonic rule, tracing the sources of the Way and virtue, and setting forth achievements, there are things that scholars such as Ma Rong and Zheng Xuan, throughout their lives, never managed to…

title: 隆慶元年順天府鄉試錄
text:
知者而佔畢小子能言之豈
其智慮懸殊哉道之隱顯異
也
明興于茲二百年矣方內乂寧
聲教四暨泝古一統之盛治
平之久無如
今日者豈非士習正而治道有
===
依賴耶迺邇者經術稍漓訛
言競熾始于一二材辨之士
沉酣張陸之說介以混同儒
釋高自標致人情厭常惡檢
靡然從之雖道體如日中天
無損浮翳第恐作心害政為
士習世道病不淺耳茲諸士

明興于茲二百年矣，方內乂寧，聲教四暨。泝古一統之盛、治平之久，無如今日者，豈非士習正而治道有依賴耶？迺邇者經術稍漓，訛言競熾，始于一二材辨之士，沉酣張陸之說，介以混同儒釋，高自標致。人情厭常惡檢，靡然從之。雖道體如日中天，無損浮翳，第恐作心害政，為士習世道病不淺耳。茲諸士
translation_en:
…things beyond their knowledge, yet even young students poring over texts can speak of them. Could their intelligence and understanding differ so greatly? It is the difference between the Way being obscured and being manifest.
It has now been two hundred years since the Ming arose. Within the realm there is order and peace, and its civilizing influence reaches in all directions. Looking back into antiquity, no age has equaled the present in the grandeur of its unity or the duration of its peace and good government. Is this not because scholars’ practices are correct, giving the conduct of government something upon which to depend? Yet lately, classical learning has become somewhat diluted, and erroneous teachings have competed in spreading unchecked. This began with one or two talented and eloquent scholars who steeped themselves in the doctrines of Zhang and Lu, mingling Confucian and Buddhist teachings [?] and holding themselves up as lofty exemplars. Human nature tires of the familiar and dislikes restraint, so people have followed them in droves. Although the substance of the Way is like the sun at midday, unharmed by drifting clouds, I fear that these teachings may unsettle people’s minds and injure government, doing no slight damage to scholars’ practices and the moral order of the world. Now these scholars…

title: 隆慶元年順天府鄉試錄
text:
抱藝而來有由鄕學游郡邑
學者亦有游國學者觀其言
雖人自爲談大要不詭于孔
氏守程朱正訓將其心之不
見異物遷耶抑真見其然雖
有異聞不爲所惑耶果爾則
甚善矣如其多岐迷適飾言
===
非心諸所云云姑求不失有
司之尺寸已爾即此念已不
可與適道不可與事君矣多
士慎之哉誠僞一辨吾心自
明之矣舍邪由正夫豈異術
要于其所言以設誠于內而
致行之爾臣侍

抱藝而來，有由鄕學游郡邑學者，亦有游國學者。觀其言，雖人自爲談，大要不詭于孔氏，守程朱正訓。將其心之不見異物遷耶？抑真見其然，雖有異聞，不爲所惑耶？果爾，則甚善矣。如其多岐迷適，飾言非心，諸所云云，姑求不失有司之尺寸已爾，即此念已不可與適道，不可與事君矣。多士慎之哉！誠僞一辨，吾心自明之矣。舍邪由正，夫豈異術？要于其所言，以設誠于內而致行之爾。
臣侍
translation_en:
…have come bringing their learning. Some have proceeded from local schools to study in prefectural or county schools; others have studied at the Directorate of Education. Examining their words, although each speaks in his own way, one finds that in their essentials they do not depart from Confucius and adhere to the correct teachings of Cheng and Zhu. Is it that their minds have never been swayed by extraneous things? Or have they truly perceived the truth of these teachings, so that even when they hear divergent views, they are not misled? If so, that is very good indeed. But if, bewildered by many paths, they do not know which to follow, and embellish their words contrary to their hearts, saying all these things merely to avoid falling short of the examiners’ standards, then this very intention already makes them unfit to proceed along the Way or to serve their sovereign. You scholars, take heed! Once sincerity and falsity are distinguished, our own hearts will clearly recognize them. What special method is needed to abandon error and follow what is correct? All that is required is to hold oneself to one’s words, establish sincerity within, and put those words into practice.
Your servant attends…

講幄，仰見我皇上留意經術，作新化理，將以皇極之道敷錫萬方。夫龍興雲從，聖作物覩，多士固豐芑之詒，而適舉于是時也。異日者，樹勛弼化，以顯佑表正之烈，安知其不在茲乎？
記曰：「耆欲將至，有開必先；天降時雨，山川出雲。」誠動機應，有不偶然者。多士其思所以自獻成信，以彝訓皇極，俉正學宣明，自畿甸始。詩曰：「思皇多士，生此王國。王國克生，維周之楨。」又曰：「商邑翼…」
translation_en:
…attending in the imperial lecture chamber, I look up and see that Our Emperor devotes his attention to classical learning and renews governance through moral transformation, intending to extend the Way of the Sovereign’s Standard as a blessing to every region. When the dragon rises, clouds follow; when the sage arises, all things behold him. These many scholars are indeed the legacy of nurturing talent for posterity, evoked by the luxuriant millet, and they happen to be selected at this very time. Who can know that those who will one day establish merit and assist the imperial work of transformation, displaying the achievements of aiding their sovereign and setting things right by example, are not among them?
The Record of Rites says: “When a long-cherished desire is about to be fulfilled, an opening must first appear; when Heaven sends timely rain, mountains and rivers bring forth clouds.” When sincerity moves and the incipient workings respond, this is no mere coincidence. Let these many scholars consider how to offer themselves in complete trustworthiness, taking enduring precepts and the Sovereign’s Standard as their guide, so that [?] orthodox learning may be proclaimed and clarified, beginning in the metropolitan region. The Book of Odes says: “Majestic are the many scholars, born in this royal realm. The royal realm indeed brings them forth: they are the pillars of Zhou.” It also says: “The city of Shang, stately…”
